title: Q1 2025 account churn rate
prompt: What fraction of accounts with an active subscription at the start of Q1 2025 had no active subscription by the end of the quarter?
population: Accounts with a subscription active on 2025-01-01 (started_at on or before that date, and ended_at is null or after it).
metricDefinition: accounts active on 2025-01-01 with no subscription active on 2025-04-01, divided by accounts active on 2025-01-01.
transformationPlan: find accounts with a subscription active on 2025-01-01
find accounts with a subscription active on 2025-04-01
count accounts in the first set but not the second
divide by the size of the first set
referenceSql: WITH active_start AS (SELECT DISTINCT account_id FROM subscriptions WHERE started_at <= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' AND (ended_at IS NULL OR ended_at > TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01')), active_end AS (SELECT DISTINCT account_id FROM subscriptions WHERE started_at <= TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01' AND (ended_at IS NULL OR ended_at > TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01')) SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE a.account_id NOT IN (SELECT account_id FROM active_end))::DOUBLE / count(*) AS q1_churn_rate FROM active_start a

commonWrongAnswers.sql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'canceled')::DOUBLE / count(*) FROM subscriptions WHERE started_at <= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
commonWrongAnswers.whyWrong: Uses the subscription's current status flag instead of checking whether the account had ANY active subscription by quarter-end — an account that canceled one plan but started a new one isn't actually churned.
